Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple, well-defined pulmonary nodules of varying sizes (some up to 3 cm) that are predominantly located in the lower lung zones without obvious calcification. This specific radiographic pattern is characteristic of necrotizing sarcoid granulomatosis (NSG), distinguishing it from classic sarcoidosis (typically upper/mid-zone with lymphadenopathy) or tuberculosis.
